# Applying to SPAN & application review

Description of the flow from **public application** through **dashboard review**: no login is required to apply; review and status changes happen in the dashboard for members with the applications permission.

---

## 1\. Applicant side: how someone applies

**What happens:** A visitor goes to the SPAN homepage and scrolls to the **“Join Our Movement”** section (or clicks “Join Our Movement” / “Get Involved,” which scroll to `#join`). There they see the application form: name, email, phone, grade, school, state, hours per week, referral source, optional LinkedIn/Instagram, optional resume upload, and additional info.

They submit with **no account** as we don’t ask them to log in, of course. The form posts their data to the database and, if they attached a resume, uploads the file to storage. After a successful submission, they see a success message; we don’t email the applicant at this step yet. **Leadership** receives a **Resend** alert (Edge Function `notify-new-application`) with applicant summary and a link to the dashboard Applications section. Default recipients: Joel, Vishank, Ben, and Shayan (`@spanationwide.org`); override with Supabase secret `APPLICATION_NOTIFY_TO` (comma-separated).

**Where it lives:**

- **Page:** The form is on the **homepage**. `HomePage.jsx` renders the main sections and includes `<ApplicationForm />` in the “Join Our Movement” block (around the `#join` anchor).  
- **Component:** All form logic and submission live in **`src/components/ApplicationForm.jsx`**.

**How submission works (technical):**

- The form uses a **separate, anonymous** Supabase client (created inside `ApplicationForm.jsx`) so that we never send an authenticated session. That way the submission is truly public and doesn’t depend on anyone being logged in.  
- **Resume (optional):** If the user picks a file, the component uploads it to the **`applications-resumes`** storage bucket in Supabase, with a safe filename (timestamp \+ sanitized name), then stores that filename in the application row.  
- **Database:** One row is inserted into **`applications`** with `status: 'pending'`. Fields include `email`, `phone_number`, `full_name`, `grade`, `school`, `state`, `hours_per_week`, `referral_source`, `linkedin_url`, `instagram_url`, `resume_file`, `additional_info`, etc. There is no link to a member or auth user yet — that comes when an exec creates a member later.  
- **RLS:** A migration allows **anonymous inserts** on `applications` (and a policy so the insert can succeed and the client can read back the inserted row if needed). Only this table is written to by unauthenticated users; everything else requires a logged-in member.

---

## 2\. Reviewing applications

**What happens:** Members who have the **applications** permission (and in practice, execs who have all four permissions) see an **Applications** section in the dashboard. They can filter by status: All, Pending, Invited, Met with, Onboard, Accepted, Rejected. The list includes an internal **review score** (numeric, optional). Clicking a row opens a detail modal with the applicant’s info, notes, review score editor, and resume link (if any). See figure.

![][image1]  
![][image2]  
*Figure: viewing a ‘mock’ application (named john doe) I submitted with my alt. email*

From the modal they can:

- **Mark Invited (email):** Opens a **preview** of the interview invitation (from Joel’s address on `spanationwide.org`, Vishank CC’d). Confirming **sends** the email via Resend and sets status to **Invited** (no separate “invite without email” path).  
- **Mark Met with:** Choose a date, then status becomes **met_with** (workflow only; no account yet).  
- **Mark Onboard (email):** Same preview/send pattern as the invite, using **`send-onboarding-schedule-email`**: congratulates the applicant and asks for availability over the next two weeks to schedule the **onboarding call**; then status becomes **Onboard**.  
- **Set a review score** (optional numeric value, e.g. 1, 2.5) stored as `numeric_grade`, separate from the applicant’s school grade.  
- **AI text screening:** Dashboard can run DivEye / ScreenComply checks on application **additional info** (and related proposal checks elsewhere) to help flag low-quality or AI-generated text before human review — advisory signal, not an auto-reject.  
- **Add or edit notes** (stored on the application) for other execs to see.  
- **Accept:** The application is marked `accepted`, and the **Add Member** modal opens with the application’s data pre-filled so the exec can create the new member in the next step (covered in the next section).  
- **Reject:** The application is marked `rejected`. The exec can optionally **send a rejection email** to the applicant (see below). 

**Where it lives:**

- All of this is in **`src/pages/DashboardPage.jsx`**. The Applications section is conditionally shown when the current member has the `applications` permission. The same file holds the application list, filters, modal, and handlers for status updates, accept, and reject.  
- Applications are loaded with `supabase.from('applications').select(...)` in a `loadApplications`\-style function (called when the dashboard loads and when the exec has the right permission).

**Data:**

- **Table:** `applications`. Key columns for this flow: `status` (pending → invited → met\_with → onboard → accepted | rejected), `numeric_grade` (optional internal score), `reviewed_by` (member\_id of the exec who last updated), `reviewed_at`, `notes`, `met_with_at`, optional **`referral_friend_name`** (when referral source is friend/classmate). Applicant school grade is in `grade` (text). Resume filename is in `resume_file`; the modal links to the file in the **`applications-resumes`** bucket.  
- **Who can see:** RLS allows only members with the appropriate permission to read applications; the dashboard only shows the Applications section when the member has `applications` permission.

**Things to know:** Accepting an application doesn’t create the member by itself — it opens the member-creation form with the application data imported. The actual creation (Auth user \+ `members` row \+ welcome email) is the next section. Rejection email is optional and goes through an Edge Function.

---

## 3\. Interview invitation email (pending → invited)

**What happens:** When an exec chooses **Mark Invited (email)** on a **pending** application, the dashboard loads a preview from **`send-invitation-email`** (`dry_run: true`), then on confirm sends via Resend and updates the row to `invited`.

**Where it lives:**

- **Frontend:** `DashboardPage.jsx` — preview modal, then POST without `dry_run`.  
- **Backend:** **`supabase/functions/send-invitation-email/index.ts`**. Same exec check as rejection email. Optional secrets: `INVITATION_FROM`, `INVITATION_CC`.

---

## 4\. Rejection email (backend)

**What happens:** When an exec rejects an application and leaves “Send rejection email” checked, the dashboard calls an Edge Function that sends a single email to the applicant (e.g. “Thank you for your interest; we’re not moving forward at this time”) from SPAN’s domain.

**Where it lives:**

- **Frontend:** `DashboardPage.jsx` sends a POST request to the edge function endpoint. The application is already updated to be `rejected` before this call.  
- **Backend:** **`supabase/functions/send-rejection-email/index.ts`**. It checks that the user calling it is logged in and that their `members` row has all four permissions (exec). If so, it uses Resend to send the email. The API key and “from” address are configured in Supabase (secrets / env), not in the repo.

---

## 5\. Summary flow

| Step | Who | What |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| 1 | Visitor | Fills application form on homepage (no login). Data → `applications` (status `pending`). Optional resume → `applications-resumes` bucket. |
| 2 | Exec | Sees Applications in dashboard, filters by status, opens application modal. |
| 3 | Exec | **Invited** via invitation email preview + send; **Met with** / **Onboard** via status buttons; add notes and optional review score (`numeric_grade`). |
| 4a | Exec | **Accept** → application set to `accepted`, Add Member modal opens with application data pre-filled (member is created in the next workflow step). |
| 4b | Exec | **Reject** → application set to `rejected`; optionally send rejection email via Edge Function. |

Next in the flow: **Adding a new member** — the exec fills out or confirms the member form (including importing from the accepted application), submits, and that creates the Auth user, `members` row, and triggers the welcome email.
